ukmt-stmc-2014-15-final-shuttle-a1.title: Cancel factorials
ukmt-stmc-2014-15-final-shuttle-a1.body:
$\dfrac{7!\times 3!}{4!}\times\dfrac{5!}{6!\times3!}=\dfrac{7!}{6!}\times\dfrac{5!}{4!}\times\dfrac{3!}{3!}=7\times5=35$.

Five less than this is $30$. (In the original shuttle round $30$ was passed on to A2.)

**Answer: $30$**

ukmt-stmc-2014-15-final-shuttle-a2.title: Binary representation
ukmt-stmc-2014-15-final-shuttle-a2.body:
(In the contest $T=30$ was the answer passed on from A1.) $30=16+8+4+2$ is $11110$ in binary, which has four $1$s. Any way of writing a number as a sum of $k$ powers of $2$ can be turned into its binary form by repeatedly merging equal powers, which reduces $k$; so $k\ge4$, and with exactly four terms no merging can occur: the terms are $2^1,2^2,2^3,2^4$. Hence $m+n+p+q=1+2+3+4=10$.

**Answer: $10$**

ukmt-stmc-2014-15-final-shuttle-a3.title: Compute both times
ukmt-stmc-2014-15-final-shuttle-a3.body:
(In the contest $T=10$ was passed on from A2.) The distance is $40$ miles. Alan: $\frac{40}{50}=0.8$ h $=2880$ s. Bob: $\frac{20}{60}+\frac{20}{40}=\frac13+\frac12=\frac56$ h $=3000$ s. The difference is $120$ s.

**Answer: $120$ seconds**

ukmt-stmc-2014-15-final-shuttle-a4.title: List the cubes
ukmt-stmc-2014-15-final-shuttle-a4.body:
(In the contest $T=120$ came from A3.) The cubes below $120$ are $1,8,27,64$.

- $C=1$: $P+S=1$ is impossible.
- $C=8$: $S=1$ gives $P=7$ (prime). $S=4$ gives $4$, no.
- $C=27$: $S=1,4,9,16,25$ give $P=26,23,18,11,2$: primes $23,11,2$ (three solutions).
- $C=64$: $S=1,4,9,16,25,36,49$ give $63,60,55,48,39,28,15$: none prime.

Total: $1+3=4$ solutions.

**Answer: $4$**

ukmt-stmc-2014-15-final-shuttle-b1.title: Shift the roots
ukmt-stmc-2014-15-final-shuttle-b1.body:
$4x^2-12x+5=(2x-1)(2x-5)$ has roots $\frac12$ and $\frac52$. The roots of the first equation are each $3$ less: $-\frac52$ and $-\frac12$ (both different and each 3 less than a root). Their product is $\frac b4=\frac54$, so $b=5$.

**Answer: $5$**

ukmt-stmc-2014-15-final-shuttle-b1.title: Substitute
ukmt-stmc-2014-15-final-shuttle-b1.body:
If $y=x+3$ solves the second equation then $x$ solves $4(x+3)^2-12(x+3)+5=0$, i.e. $4x^2+12x+5=0$. So $a=12$, $b=5$.

**Answer: $5$**

ukmt-stmc-2014-15-final-shuttle-b2.title: Maximise $d-a$
ukmt-stmc-2014-15-final-shuttle-b2.body:
(In the contest $T=5$ came from B1.) Let the integers be $a\le b\le c\le d$. Sum $=20$; median $\frac{b+c}2=6$ so $b+c=12$ and $a+d=8$. To maximise $d-a$ take $a$ as small as possible: $a=1$, $d=7$. We need $b\le c$ with $b+c=12$ and $1\le b\le c\le 7$: $b=5$, $c=7$ works. The range is $7-1=6$.

**Answer: $6$**

ukmt-stmc-2014-15-final-shuttle-b3.title: Evaluate
ukmt-stmc-2014-15-final-shuttle-b3.body:
(In the contest $T=6$ came from B2.) $16^{3/4}=8$, $8^{-2/3}=\frac14$, $4^{1/2}=2$, so the numerator is $8\cdot\frac14\cdot2=4$. The denominator is $8^{-5/3}=\frac1{32}$. Hence $x=4\times32=128$ and the digit sum is $1+2+8=11$.

**Answer: $11$**

ukmt-stmc-2014-15-final-shuttle-b4.title: Cone dimensions
ukmt-stmc-2014-15-final-shuttle-b4.body:
(In the contest $T=11$ came from B3.) The radius is $10$ cm. The arc length is $\frac{216}{360}\cdot2\pi\cdot10=12\pi$, which becomes the circumference of the cone's base, so the base radius is $6$. The slant height is $10$, so the height is $\sqrt{100-36}=8$. Volume $=\frac13\pi\cdot36\cdot8=96\pi$.

**Answer: $k=96$**

ukmt-stmc-2014-15-final-shuttle-c1.title: Midpoint and slope
ukmt-stmc-2014-15-final-shuttle-c1.body:
The midpoint is $(9,1)$ and the segment has gradient $\frac{4-(-2)}{10-8}=3$, so the perpendicular bisector has gradient $-\frac13$: $y-1=-\frac13(x-9)$, i.e. $3y=-x+12$. Hence $\frac cb=\frac{12}{3}=4$ (the ratio does not depend on scaling).

**Answer: $4$**

ukmt-stmc-2014-15-final-shuttle-c2.title: Common base
ukmt-stmc-2014-15-final-shuttle-c2.body:
(In the contest $T=4$ came from C1.) $9^{2x}=3^{4x}$ and $\left(\frac13\right)^5=3^{-5}$, so $4x=-5$, $x=-\frac54$. Then $a-b=5-4=1$.

**Answer: $1$**

ukmt-stmc-2014-15-final-shuttle-c3.title: Angle sum
ukmt-stmc-2014-15-final-shuttle-c3.body:
(In the contest $T=1$ came from C2.) The angles are $170^\circ,50^\circ,4x,3x,x$, summing to $(5-2)\cdot180=540$. So $8x=320$ and $x=40$.

**Answer: $40$**

ukmt-stmc-2014-15-final-shuttle-c4.title: Equilateral triangle
ukmt-stmc-2014-15-final-shuttle-c4.body:
(In the contest $T=40$ came from C3.) $\angle AOD=60^\circ$. Since $OD\perp AB$, $D$ is the midpoint of $AB$ and $\angle BOD=\angle AOD=60^\circ$. Now $C$ lies on ray $OD$, so $\angle BOC=60^\circ$ and $OB=OC$, hence triangle $OBC$ is equilateral with side $5$: the radius is $5$.

Then $OD=5\cos60^\circ=2.5$, $DC=5-2.5=2.5$, $BD=5\sin60^\circ=\frac{5\sqrt3}2$. Area of $BCD=\frac12\cdot BD\cdot DC=\frac12\cdot\frac{5\sqrt3}2\cdot\frac52=\frac{25\sqrt3}8$.

**Answer: $\frac{25\sqrt3}{8}$ cm$^2$**

ukmt-stmc-2014-15-final-shuttle-d2.title: Angle sum
ukmt-stmc-2014-15-final-shuttle-d2.body:
(In the contest $T=11$ came from D1.) The common difference is $20^\circ$. The six angles sum to $720^\circ$: $6A+20(0+1+2+3+4+5)=6A+300=720$, so $A=70$ and $A-10=60$.

**Answer: $60$**

ukmt-stmc-2014-15-final-shuttle-d4.title: Scale factors
ukmt-stmc-2014-15-final-shuttle-d4.body:
(In the contest $T=4$ came from D3.) The larger radius is $10$ cm. Surface areas are in ratio $1:4$ so lengths are in ratio $1:2$ and the smaller radius is $5$ cm. A solid hemisphere of radius $r$ has volume $\frac23\pi r^3$. Difference $=\frac23\pi(1000-125)=\frac{1750\pi}3$ cm$^3$.

**Answer: $\frac{1750\pi}{3}$ cm$^3$**
